title: How to prepare for your first snowboard lesson
description: What to do a week before, the evening before and on the morning of your first snowboard lesson: fitness, clothing, rental, food and what to tell your instructor.
text: Prepare for your first snowboard lesson in advance: a week before, do simple leg and balance exercises; the evening before, pack warm waterproof clothing and get a good night's sleep; in the morning, eat a proper breakfast and arrive early enough for rental. Tell your instructor about your experience, injuries and fears. In short Your first lesson goes more smoothly when your body is ready for the effort, your clothes stay dry and your equipment is sorted before the lesson starts. Here is a day by day plan. A week before: get your body ready Snowboarding works your thighs, glutes, core and ankles. If you have not exercised for a while, spend 10–15 minutes a day for 5–7 days before the trip on: squats and lunges; planks on straight arms and on forearms; standing on one leg with your eyes closed; a light hamstring stretch. The goal is not to build muscle but to keep your legs from tiring out in the first hour. The evening before: clothes and documents Pack in layers: a thermal base layer, a warm mid layer and a waterproof jacket and trousers. Avoid cotton: it gets wet and makes you cold. Bring a spare pair of gloves or mittens. Check that you have: an ID document rental shops may ask for one ; a charger or power bank: phones drain faster in the cold; sunscreen and lip balm; ski goggles or sunglasses. The full list is in our article "What to bring to the mountains of Almaty" /en/guides/what to bring to the mountains almaty/ . In the morning: breakfast and time Eat a proper breakfast: you burn energy faster in the cold and at altitude. Bring water and a snack. Leave enough time for the journey, the rental queue and changing, so you do not start the lesson tired and stressed. Rental: how to tell the gear fits What to check How it should be Boots Your heel does not lift when you lean forward; toes lightly touch the front Board length For a beginner, usually between chin and nose height Bindings They close without force and the straps are not twisted Helmet It does not wobble when you tilt your head and does not press If something rubs or hurts, say so at the rental shop straight away, not an hour later on the slope. What to tell your instructor A good instructor will ask, but it helps to mention up front: whether you have tried snowboarding, skiing, skateboarding or surfing; any knee, back or wrist injuries; what scares you: speed, lifts, falling; what you want to achieve by the end of the day. During the lesson Drink water, take short breaks and say honestly when you are tired. Mistakes and falls on day one are normal. Getting your stopping right matters more than rushing into turns. After the lesson Do a light stretch in the evening and get enough sleep. If you plan a second day in a row, expect sore muscles. Do not ignore sharp joint pain or a blow to the head: see a doctor. title: What to bring to the mountains of Almaty in winter: a snowboarder's checklist
description: A checklist of clothing, protection, documents and small items for a day on the slopes near Almaty, plus a separate list for off-piste days.
text: For a day of riding in the mountains near Almaty, bring layered clothing thermal base layer, fleece, waterproof shell , a helmet, goggles, two pairs of gloves, sunscreen, water, a snack and a charged phone. For off piste riding you also need an avalanche transceiver, shovel and probe, the skills to use them and a guide. In short Weather in the mountains above Almaty changes faster than in the city: hot in the sun, cold in the shade and wind. So the main rule is layers you can easily take off and put on. Below is a list for a normal resort day and a separate list for off piste riding. Clothing: three layers Layer What works What to avoid Base Synthetic or merino wool thermal underwear A cotton T shirt Mid A fleece or light down jacket A thick jumper that does not dry Outer Waterproof membrane jacket and trousers Jeans and a city jacket Add warm socks one pair, not two: a second pair squeezes your foot in the boot , a neck gaiter or balaclava, and a thin hat under the helmet if the helmet is loose. Protection A helmet is a must. Ski goggles: on sunny days the snow is blinding, and on cloudy days goggles help you see the terrain. Impact shorts and knee pads for beginners. Wrist guards while you are learning. Small things people forget High SPF sunscreen and lip balm: UV is stronger at altitude. Water and a snack. A power bank: phones drain faster in the cold. Spare gloves. Cash and a card. An ID document for rental. For children Children need the same layers, plus spare mittens and socks. Check that the helmet fits and is fastened. We discuss the details of kids' sessions with parents when booking. For off piste days Riding outside groomed runs comes with avalanche risk. On top of the usual list you need: an avalanche transceiver beacon , shovel and probe for every rider; the skills to use them, practised in advance rather than on the day; a backpack that fits this gear; a guide who knows the area and follows the avalanche situation. Before you go, check the weather forecast, Kazhydromet's report on snow conditions in the mountains and any avalanche warnings from the Ministry of Emergency Situations. The guide makes the final call on the route on the spot. Checklist before you leave home Three layers of clothing with a waterproof outer layer Helmet and goggles Gloves and a spare pair Sunscreen and lip balm Water, snack, power bank ID and money Questions about gear or the lesson format? Ask us /en/contact/ .

title: How to start snowboarding in Almaty
description: A beginner plan for snowboarding in Almaty: how to learn, whether you need an instructor, what a first lesson covers and what to check before you go.
text: To start snowboarding in Almaty you need warm waterproof clothing, a helmet and one or two lessons with an instructor on a gentle learning slope. Beginners are better off renting a board and boots. The closest large resort to the city is Shymbulak, above Medeu. Check opening hours, prices and slope conditions on the resort's official website on the day you go. In short Start with the basics rather than trying to turn straight away. On day one a beginner learns to stand on the board, stop, and slide down sideways the "falling leaf" . Linked turns come later, at a different pace for everyone. Learning with an instructor is easier: they correct your stance right away and show you how to fall safely. Step 1. Choose how to learn Format Who it suits What to keep in mind Private lesson People who want to learn faster or are nervous about falling The instructor focuses only on you, but it costs more Group course People learning with friends or who enjoy company The group should be at the same level On your own People with ski or skateboard experience Higher risk of bad habits and injury Almaty Snowboard School offers private lessons, group courses and kids training; we share durations and prices on request. Ask us on the contact page /en/contact/ . Step 2. Sort out equipment There is no need to buy a board before your first lessons. A soft, short rental board suits beginners. Boots should hold your heel firmly without squeezing your toes. A helmet is a must; impact shorts and knee pads make early falls much softer. Step 3. Pick the day and the slope A first lesson needs a gentle, quiet learning area. Weekdays are usually calmer than weekends. Before you go, check: that the lift to the learning slope is running; the weather forecast and visibility; current lift pass prices on the resort's website. We do not publish resort schedules or prices because they change. Check the official website on the day. Step 4. Find your stance "Regular" means left foot forward, "goofy" means right foot forward. A quick test: stand still and ask someone to give you a gentle push from behind. The foot you step forward with is probably your front foot. Your instructor will confirm it on the slope. Step 5. First drills A typical first lesson goes like this: 1. Walking and climbing with one foot strapped in. 2. Gliding straight on an almost flat area. 3. Stopping on an edge and sliding down on the heel and toe edges. 4. The "falling leaf": zigzagging down without switching edges. If you can stop confidently on both edges by the end of the day, that is a good result. Common beginner mistakes Looking at your feet instead of where you are going. Leaning back away from the slope, which shoots the board forward. Putting your hands out when you fall. It is safer to land on your forearms or bottom with your chin tucked. Riding until you are exhausted. Tired legs make more mistakes, so it is better to stop early. What next After a basic lesson you can continue privately or in a group.
